HOW TO READ THE MAP

Brighter colours indicate higher aurora probability. The oval shifts poleward during quiet periods (Kp 1–3) and expands toward the equator as geomagnetic activity increases (Kp 5–9).

ABOUT THE AURORA

What Causes Aurora?

The Sun emits a constant stream of charged particles — the solar wind. During solar flares and CMEs, these particles reach Earth's magnetosphere and spiral down magnetic field lines toward the poles, colliding with atmospheric oxygen and nitrogen to produce light.

100–300 km altitude where aurora forms

The Kp Index Explained

The Planetary K-index (Kp) measures global geomagnetic activity on a scale of 0–9, updated every 3 hours. Kp 5+ triggers the G-scale storm thresholds. The higher the Kp, the further from the poles aurora extends — a Kp 9 storm in May 2024 made aurora visible worldwide.

Kp 5 minimum for mid-latitude visibility

Why Bz Matters

The north-south component of the interplanetary magnetic field (IMF Bz) is the single most important real-time indicator. When Bz turns southward (negative), Earth's magnetic field opens up via reconnection, letting solar particles flood in. The stronger the negative Bz, the better the aurora.

−20 nT Bz for a major aurora event

AURORA COLORS

Green Oxygen · 100–150 km Most common color
Red Oxygen · 200–300 km Rare high-altitude
Blue / Violet Nitrogen · 80–100 km Lower edge fringe
Pink / Mauve N₂ + O mix · 90 km Active substorms
Purple Nitrogen ions · 80 km Deep curtain base
STEVE Sub-Auroral Ion Drift Mauve ribbon east–west

VIEWING TIPS

🌑

Dark Sky

Travel at least 20 km from city lights. Even a small town can wash out a faint aurora display. Use Light Pollution Map to find dark sites.

🕚

Best Hours

Geomagnetic substorms peak around local magnetic midnight — typically 10 pm to 2 am. Set an alert and get outside when Kp rises above your latitude threshold.

👁️

Dark-Adapt

Allow 20–30 minutes for your eyes to fully adjust to the dark. Avoid looking at your phone screen — use red-light mode if you must. The difference is dramatic.

📷

Camera Trick

Take a 5-second photo even if you can't see anything. Camera sensors detect the green 557.7 nm wavelength better than the human eye — you might be surprised what's there.

❄️

Face North

In the northern hemisphere, look toward magnetic north (slightly west of true north in most locations). The auroral arc rises from the northern horizon during moderate activity.

⚡

Watch Bz

Monitor the live Kp bar above. When Bz goes strongly negative (−10 nT or more) and holds there, get outside fast — that's your 15–60 minute warning from the DSCOVR satellite.
